subject: Request: SDK routing hint + telemetry hooks for contracted capacity
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SDK routing hint + telemetry hooks for contracted capacity

Hi Karthik / Marcus,

BrightLane (prospect) surfaced an interesting ask during today's technical discovery: they want to preferentially route a subset of requests to their reserved/dedicated capacity (contracted GPUs) but keep using our hosted API surface. Their sales/infra constraints require an "honor contract" flag from the SDK so that the request is routed to their reserved pool when available, with explicit server-side ack codes and telemetry so they can detect fallback to on-demand capacity.

Key asks from the BrightLane call: 
- SDK-level optional param: routing_hint: "contracted"|"best-effort"
- Server-side response header / code that indicates: ROUTE=CONTRACTED | ROUTE=ON_DEMAND | ROUTE=FALLBACK
- Telemetry hook in SDK to emit trace id + route outcome for each request (they will ingest to their APM)
- Backward-compatible behavior: default = best-effort (no change)

Attachments: I captured a minimal sample request they sent (brightlane-sample-req.json) and a trace of a fallback we observed during yesterday's demo (route-fallback-trace.txt). Also CC'ing Marissa to keep sales <> product timelines aligned.

Can you confirm feasibility and a rough engineering estimate? BrightLane is asking for an implementation window within the next 6 weeks if possible (SOW is close).

Thanks,
Logan
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDK routing hint + telemetry hooks for contracted capacity

Thanks for the context and the attached artifacts, Logan. Quick thoughts from runtime perspective:

- routing_hint param is straightforward to accept at the API gateway layer. We'll need to decide enforcement semantics: strictly pin to contracted pool (reject if unavailable) vs. soft preference with explicit fallback event.
- Emitting a ROUTE response header and a structured numeric code should be easy; we already annotate traces with node assignment. We'll need to standardize the header name (e.g., X-Redwood-Route) and codes.
- Telemetry hook: the SDK can surface an event callback and a structured log output (json line) with fields: request_id, trace_id, route, latency_ms. We should keep the hook opt-in and low-overhead.

Questions:
1) Do we need an option to make the routing_hint enforced (reject vs fallback) or is soft-preference acceptable?
2) If BrightLane plans to rely on strict pinning for regulatory reasons, we need an SLA + capacity reservation enforcement path, which touches provisioning/allocator.

I can prototype the header + SDK callback in ~2 engineer-weeks (one backend, one SDK) for PoC. Production-ready rollout (tests, rollout policy, docs) ~6-8 weeks depending on priority. Marcus, can you weigh in on allocator impact?

-Karthik

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDK routing hint + telemetry hooks for contracted capacity

On Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 11:03 AM Karthik Iyer wrote:
> I can prototype the header + SDK callback in ~2 engineer-weeks (one backend, one SDK) for PoC. Production-ready rollout (tests, rollout policy, docs) ~6-8 weeks depending on priority. Marcus, can you weigh in on allocator impact?

Short version: impact depends on enforcement semantics.

- Soft-preference (honor if available, otherwise fallback): minimal allocator changes. We already have routing tiers and fallback; we'd surface the choice and increment a metric to track frequency of contracted->on-demand fallbacks.
- Strict pinning (reject/queue if contracted capacity unavailable): requires new admission control and queueing policy for reserved pools, can increase tail latency for pinned requests; needs capacity accounting changes and a potential SLA exception approval.

For BrightLane SOW I'm assuming soft-preference is acceptable unless they explicitly require hard isolation. That keeps implementation small and low-risk. If they need hard pinning, we should escalate to pricing/ops + legal (SLA implications).

I'll support a PoC within the 2-week window Karthik mentioned; will need one runtime engineer and a test harness to replay the brightlane-sample-req.json to validate route header emission.

-Marcus
Senior Engineer, Runtime

From: Julia Park <julia@brightlane.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@brightlane.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDK routing hint + telemetry hooks for contracted capacity

Thanks Logan — quick confirmation from our side. BrightLane is primarily looking for: 
1) A way to bias requests to our reserved capacity (soft preference is fine initially).
2) Clear signal when a request falls back so our observability can mark it and gate cost/latency metrics.
3) Minimal change to our app: we'd rather flip an SDK flag than run separate endpoints.

Attached is the sample snippet we ran in the demo where a warm-contracted request still landed on on-demand (route-fallback-trace.txt). The SOW (SOW_BrightLane-v2.pdf) references a 6-week deliverable window for the feature. We're flexible to accept a staged rollout with PoC + GA.

Happy to jump on a quick call with Karthik/Marcus if that helps narrow acceptance criteria.

Best,
Julia Park
Head of Integrations
BrightLane Solutions

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SDK routing hint + telemetry hooks for contracted capacity

Thanks all — summary and next steps: 
- Scope: implement SDK optional param routing_hint (values: contracted|best-effort), emit X-Redwood-Route header on response, and add SDK callback hook for telemetry. Default behavior = best-effort (no change).
- Enforcement: proceed with soft-preference for PoC. We will not attempt strict pinning unless BrightLane requests it formally in writing and Ops signs off.
- Timeline: Karthik + Marcus to spin a PoC branch: 2 weeks for PoC + internal test harness. Marissa to communicate tentative shipment date to BrightLane and update SOW if needed.
- Acceptance criteria for PoC: header appears for each request, SDK callback receives {request_id, trace_id, route, latency_ms}, and sample harness shows < 1% unexpected fallbacks in a controlled replay.

Marissa — can you propose a customer-facing acceptance test and a short FAQ for sales to use? Karthik/Marcus — please add a minimal RFC in the runtime repo and tag for review. I'll loop in product if we hit roadblocks on SLA/terms.

Logan
